options.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025 certification training narrative, printed page 51, partial charge and pressurized leak check (PDF page 57); not review questions; MACS January 2025 certification training narrative, printed page 18, limited leak-test charge versus compressor operation (PDF page 24); not review questions
options.support: In the staged procedure described in the training narrative, the partial charge supplies pressure for evaporator leak checking before the balance is delivered. Robinair AC1234-6 Rev F also describes a partial charge for leak checking. It is not the full operating charge or a way to determine capacity or test compressor performance. Machine behavior following a failed vacuum check varies between these sources; follow the actual machine instructions.

options.text: Circulating oil for checking compressor performance
options.sourcePassageLocator: MACS January 2025 certification training narrative, printed page 51, partial charge and pressurized leak check (PDF page 57); not review questions; MACS January 2025 certification training narrative, printed page 18, limited leak-test charge versus compressor operation (PDF page 24); not review questions
options.whyCandidateMightChoose: Treats a small refrigerant addition as sufficient for operating the compressor and circulating oil.
options.validOtherCondition: Compressor evaluation requires the specified charge and operating procedure.
options.whyStemExcludes: The partial test charge does not establish those operating conditions.

selectionMethod: Retain all14 targeted pilot IDs; SystemRandom sample without replacement from each remaining category until10 percategory. No filtering by previous score or distractor judgment.
sourceVariation: MACS January 2025 page 51 describes blocking recharge after vacuum-decay failure. Robinair AC1234-6 567817 Rev F pages 29–30 permits a partial test charge after a failed vacuum test to locate leaks, followed by repair and restarting checks. Do not universalize either controller sequence. The full SAE standard was not accessed; no claim that it universally mandates the floor-probe location.
